title: Add failover summary events to incident timeline for auto-populated postmortem milestones
author: Devon Price
release_notes: Incident timeline now ingests structured failover audit events and renders a concise “Failover summary” block (trigger → execute → rollback) to support auto-populated postmortem milestones and clearer dashboards/annotations.
body:
## Context
During the 2026-01-15 controlled regional failover (us-east → eu-west), we had to manually reconstruct the key milestones (trigger time, policy flip, drain start, rollback, steady-state) across multiple sources (routing audit logs, controller logs, Slack timeline notes). This PR integrates failover automation events into the incident timeline tooling so that postmortems can auto-populate those milestones and on-call can see a consistent view during an event.

This is part of the Regional Failover Automation Upgrade program and complements the new structured failover audit events (recommendation/execution/rollback) emitted by routing/control plane.

## What this changes
- Adds a new incident-timeline ingest adapter for `failover.audit_event` records emitted by the failover controller/policy engine.
- Normalizes audit events into timeline entries with stable, low-cardinality fields.
- Adds a computed “Failover summary” block to the incident timeline view that groups related events by `failover_id` and renders:
  - Trigger / corroboration signals
  - Decision outcome (recommended vs executed)
  - Policy flip details (source region, target region, tier/route scope)
  - Rollback reason + hold-down/anti-flap context (when present)
- Auto-creates postmortem milestone candidates (timestamps) for:
  - `failover_triggered_at`
  - `failover_executed_at`
  - `traffic_shift_started_at`
  - `traffic_shift_completed_at` (best-effort, derived from final execution event or “steady-state” marker)
  - `rollback_initiated_at` and `rollback_completed_at` (when applicable)
- Adds timeline annotations for dashboards via existing incident annotations pipeline (addresses INT-1149: missing annotations during test).

## Event schema expectations
This PR expects audit events shaped like the controller output from recent work:
- `event_type`: one of `failover.recommendation`, `failover.execution`, `failover.rollback`
- `failover_id`: stable id across the workflow
- `reason`: normalized enum (e.g., `reachability_loss`, `error_burn`, `capacity_exhaustion`, `manual_operator`, `hold_down_timer`)
- `source_region`, `target_region`
- `scope`: string summary (route/model/tier), not exploded labels
- `actor`: `automation` | `oncall:<handle>` (string)
- `evidence`: summarized string (no high-cardinality raw metrics)

If any fields are missing, we still emit a timeline entry with a degraded rendering and a warning badge to prevent ingest failures.

## Implementation notes
- Uses the existing timeline event bus (no new infra) and adds a dedicated parser with strict validation + best-effort fallback.
- Uses a bounded in-memory grouping window keyed by `failover_id` to generate the summary block; also stores summary text as a first-class timeline event so it’s visible even if grouping state is lost.
- Adds a small test fixture from the 2026-01-15 controlled failover (sanitized) to validate rendering and milestone extraction.
- Adds annotation emission for the key milestones so dashboards can show vertical markers (trigger/execution/rollback) aligned to the incident timeline.

## Files/areas changed (high level)
- `services/incident-timeline/ingest/failover_audit_adapter.ts` (new)
- `services/incident-timeline/model/timeline_entry.ts` (new entry kind: `FAILOVER_EVENT`)
- `services/incident-timeline/renderers/failover_summary.ts` (new)
- `services/incident-timeline/postmortem/milestone_candidates.ts` (extract failover milestones)
- `services/incident-timeline/annotations/emit.ts` (emit markers for failover milestones)
- `packages/audit-events/schemas/failover.ts` (tightened validation + enums; no new labels)

## Tests
- Unit: adapter parses all supported event types and tolerates missing optional fields.
- Unit: milestone extraction produces deterministic timestamps given an ordered set of events.
- Snapshot: summary rendering is stable and doesn’t leak high-cardinality evidence.
- Integration (local): replay fixture → timeline view shows grouped summary + annotations.

## Rollout / safety
- Feature-gated by `incident_timeline_failover_events` (default off in prod).
- When enabled, ingestion is non-blocking: parse errors are logged and dropped with a counter; they do not break the incident timeline pipeline.
- Added metrics:
  - `incident_timeline_failover_events_ingested_total{event_type}`
  - `incident_timeline_failover_events_dropped_total{reason}`
  - `incident_timeline_failover_summary_groups_active` (bounded)

## Follow-ups
- Wire in controller “steady-state” marker so `traffic_shift_completed_at` is explicit (today it’s best-effort).
- Add links from timeline entries to the failover dashboards panel and/or runbook section (pending final dashboard URLs).

## Screenshots (text-only)
- Timeline now shows: “Failover summary: us-east → eu-west (executed). Trigger: reachability_loss corroborated by 5xx burn. Policy flip: hosted/chat tier=prod. Rollback: none.”
- Postmortem draft auto-populates milestones and includes the failover summary block.

Checklist
- [x] Unit tests added/updated
- [x] Metrics added for ingest + drops
- [x] Feature flag added (default off)
- [x] Verified no new high-cardinality metric labels

Related
- Linear: ENG-2411 (umbrella), ENG-2426 (post-gameday action items)
- Jira: INT-1149 (missing annotations)

Notes for on-call
If you don’t see failover events in the incident timeline during a regional event, verify the feature flag is enabled for the incident tooling environment and check `incident_timeline_failover_events_dropped_total` in the incident-timeline service dashboard.

incident-timeline: add failover timeline entry kind and renderer
annotations: emit dashboard markers for failover milestones

review_conversation: Miles Thornton: Can we guarantee we don’t create a new cardinality sink with `scope`? Please confirm it stays as a bounded string and never becomes labels.

Devon Price (author): Yep — `scope` is stored/rendered as a plain string on the timeline entry and is explicitly excluded from metrics labels. Added a guard to truncate to 256 chars and a unit test that ensures it never becomes a tag/label.
Allison Grant: For annotations, can we emit both trigger and execution markers? Also ensure we include failover_id in the annotation text for correlation.

Devon Price (author): Added both markers (`failover_triggered_at`, `failover_executed_at`) and included `failover_id` in the annotation payload/title. Also added a counter for annotation emit failures.
Rafael Mendes: Please ensure parse failures don’t break incident timeline ingestion. During incidents we can’t afford the pipeline to jam.
Devon Price (author): Adapter is best-effort: validation errors increment `...dropped_total{reason=validation}` and return null. Pipeline continues. Added regression test for malformed event input.
Tomáš Novák: Rendering: can we make the summary block deterministic if events arrive slightly out of order? We saw that in staging with delayed reachability signals.

Devon Price (author): Sorting by `observed_at` with a stable tiebreaker on `event_id`. Also the summary block is emitted as a first-class event once per failover_id when we see the first execution/rollback, so we have a stable anchor in the timeline even if grouping state is evicted.
Miles Thornton: Looks good. Approved once the truncation guard is in.
Devon Price (author): Truncation guard + tests pushed in 9f2b1d3.
merge_outcome: Merged via squash into main by Devon Price on 2026-01-18
